title: Core meaning and module ownership
question: Which responsibilities define the core and where does optional behavior live?
context: Architecture decision recorded by the agent under the owner's explicit design delegation. Phase tasks and implementation remain deferred.
decision: Core owns tenant/context identity, tenant isolation, domain values, declarations, one authorization engine, one authority-read coordinator and one write coordinator. Scopes behavior, Audit and DevTools are complete internal modules; Filament remains an optional integration package.
rationale: AccessScope, IdentityCodec, grant uniqueness and tenant checks already share one authority meaning. Removing those invariants when a module is inactive would widen grants or change stored identities. Optional rich scope algorithms, audit persistence and generators have distinct owners and need no new Composer product.

evidence.note: The owner delegated architecture choices and required an affirmative target design.
